title: Investigate misaligned resident fragments from cudaMallocAsync during continuous batching
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary:
We are seeing long-lived, small-size GPU resident fragments that do not coalesce or get returned to the cudaMallocAsync pool during sustained continuous-batching workloads with heavy KV cache usage. The pattern is a steady RSS increase over hours despite steady request rate and no apparent application-level allocations. Fragments are misaligned relative to pool slab boundaries (frequently offset by 256-4096 bytes), suggesting an allocator-side split or metadata rounding bug interacting with our staging/pinned pools.

Observed behavior and metrics:
- Continuous-batching job (avg batch size 24, 99th latency SLO) shows GPU RSS climb of 6-9% over 6 hours on the p4d nodes.
- NVML resident and nvidia-smi show stable count of allocated buffers but increasing resident pages attributed to arenas tagged for kv-cache.
- cudaMallocAsync stats (from cuMemPoolQuery) indicate pool free bytes remain high, but residency reports include non-pool pinned pages that are not reachable from live allocations.
- Heap profiling (device-side) shows many small allocations (8KB-64KB) that are not freed in host code paths — they appear as tombstones in delayed-free queues in the async free worker.

Hypotheses:
1) Async-free worker is skipping coalescence for back-to-back frees whose addresses are not aligned exactly to slab headers due to rounding introduced by our staging allocator shim.
2) KV cache prefetcher occasionally promotes slices into a temporary pinned staging buffer that is freed on a non-synchronous CUDA stream; cudaMallocAsync's deferred free interacts with that stream ordering causing delayed actual device decommit and leaving small orphaned resident pages.
3) A fragmentation amplification bug in the multimap of free-lists where small-sized classes are promoted incorrectly into a different arena under high concurrency, leading to many micro-fragments.

Reproduction steps (internal):
1) Start a continuous-batching replica with kv-cache warmup enabled and prefix-preservation turned on.
2) Use a synthetic workload that issues a steady stream of requests with variable prompt lengths (50-1024 tokens) and request concurrency 80-120.
3) Enable allocator debug logging (ENV: RW_ALLOC_DEBUG=1) and capture cuMemPoolQuery snapshots every 5 minutes.
4) Collect nvprof/NVIDIA Nsight snapshots at 30-minute intervals and device heap dumps via cudaMemGetInfo and our custom heap-tracker.

Instrumentation we plan to add:
- Per-stream deferred-free counters stamped with allocator epoch to correlate stream ordering with deferred frees.
- Add boundary checks in the staging allocator to log when a returned pointer does not equal expected slab-aligned base plus allowed offset.
- Sample stacktraces for allocations in the 8KB-64KB range and attach to time-series for correlation with KV cache prefetch events.
- Export additional metrics to Grafana: pool_free_bytes, pool_resident_bytes, deferred_free_backlog, pinned_staging_count, kv_prefetch_inflight.

Short-term mitigations to evaluate (canary):
- Force synchronous free (cudaFreeHost + sync) path for pinned staging buffers under heavy KV-prefetch to see if RSS stabilizes (trade-off: latency spike risk).
- Add aggressive coalescing pass in the async-free worker that performs a page-level scan to merge adjacent free ranges before returning to the pool.
- Limit prefetched KV slice size + concurrency to reduce micro-allocation churn.

Long-term fixes under consideration:
- Harden allocator metadata to ensure canonical alignment before handing to cudaMallocAsync (avoid shim-induced rounding).
- Implement a periodic slab compaction job that runs off-peak to consolidate small free ranges and trigger pool-level decommit for cold pages.
- Rework staged pinned buffer lifecycle to use pinned host staging with explicit cudaStreamSynchronize points to allow deterministic free ordering.

Acceptance criteria and tests:
- Repro test: under the same synthetic workload, RSS growth should be <1% over 12 hours on canary after mitigation applied.
- Telemetry: deferred_free_backlog clears within 60s after workload changes; pool_resident_bytes tracks pool_free_bytes within 5%.
- No regression in 99th-token latency beyond 10% when applying synchronous-free fallback to a small subset of requests.

Next steps (owners):
- Liam: implement extra logging and per-stream deferred-free counters (ETA 3 days).
- Sofia: run nightly canary with synchronous-free toggle and collect 48-hour traces (ETA 5 days).
- Ravi (infra): provision 2 canary p4d replicas with workload harness and Grafana dashboard (ETA 2 days).

Notes on experiments done so far:
- Initial canary with forced synchronous free for pinned staging buffers reduced RSS drift by ~70% over 6 hours but introduced 8% increase in p95 token latency under peak.
- Sampling shows ~38% of small allocations are created by the kv-prefetch path during model warmup windows.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Synchronous frees mitigate leakage but may increase tail latency; must restrict to warmup/maintenance windows or only to canary slices.
- Aggressive compaction may contend with serving threads and cause jitter; should be scheduled with load-aware backoff.

Documentation and follow-ups:
- Add a runtime-1.20 docs note on allocator tunables (RW_ALLOC_COMPACT_INTERVAL and RW_ALLOC_FORCE_SYNC_FREE) and recommended values for high-throughput KV-heavy workloads.
- If root cause confirmed in shim rounding, open a follow-up RFC to propose design of a canonical pointer alignment policy across staging/pool layers.
updates: 2025-01-21: Instrumentation branch created (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1297). Adding per-stream deferred-free counters.

2025-01-29: Added extra logging for slab boundary mismatches; observed ~0.9% of frees with non-canonical offsets during high concurrency windows.
2025-02-05: Implemented aggressive coalescing pass prototype in branch coalesce-proto. Microbenchmarks show coalescing adds ~0.5ms overhead to async-free cycle under heavy load.
2025-02-12: Running long-run 72h canary on canary-2 cluster. Next checkpoint scheduled 2025-02-14.
